editor_autorun.words: Unity runs this code by itself in the editor, with the editor's full access, after the compile (no menu, play mode, or test run is needed)
editor_autorun.source: Unity Manual 'Running Editor script code on launch' ([InitializeOnLoad], [InitializeOnLoadMethod]); ScriptReference Callbacks.DidReloadScripts, AssetPostprocessor, AssetModificationProcessor

editor_folder.words: an editor script: it can use the whole UnityEditor API with the editor's full access when something calls it (a menu, the test runner)

effect_words.save_assets: writes every changed asset to disk
effect_words.scene_switch: opens, closes, or replaces the open scenes
effect_words.import_compile: imports assets; a changed script recompiles and editor scripts run after the reload
effect_words.enter_play: enters play mode: the scene's scripts run
effect_words.exit_play: leaves play mode: changes made during play are dropped
effect_words.compile_run: compiles C# it was given and runs it with the editor's full access
effect_words.menu_item: runs an editor menu command (that command decides what changes)
effect_words.reflection: calls a method or constructor found by reflection
effect_words.load_asset: loads assets: their deserialization, OnEnable, and OnValidate code runs
effect_words.instantiate: creates objects or components: their Reset, OnValidate, and [ExecuteAlways] code runs
effect_words.set_values: sets serialized values or properties: OnValidate or a property setter runs
effect_words.scene_edit: changes objects in memory (a scene object or an asset; they then have unsaved changes)
effect_words.simulate: steps physics: rigidbodies move and collision and trigger code runs
effect_words.send: sends data off the editor or starts a process
